The purpose is to liken the state of the Jews, in their ignorance of the Torah they possessed and its manifest signs, to the state of the donkey in its ignorance of the books of wisdom it carries. He said in (*Hidayat al-Hayara*):

Among the ignorance of [the Jews] is that when Harun (ʿalayhi al-salām) died and Musa buried him, the Children of Israel said to Musa: "You killed him; you envied him for his character and gentleness, because of the Children of Israel's love for him." He said: They chose seventy men from the Children of Israel, and they stood at the grave of Harun. Musa said: "O Harun, were you killed or did you die?" He said: "I died, and no one killed me."

So it is enough of the ignorance and harshness of this nation that they accused their Prophet and attributed to him the killing of his brother. Musa said: "I did not kill him," but they did not believe him until he made them hear his words, and his brother cleared him of what they had accused him of.

Among their ignorance is that Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, likened them, in their carrying of the Torah while lacking understanding of it and failing to act by it, to a donkey carrying books. In this comparison are several aspects of rebuke for their ignorance, among them:

That the donkey is among the most dull of animals, and is proverbially cited for dullness.

Another: that if it carried something other than books, such as food, fodder or water, it would have some awareness of it.

Another: that when they were burdened with it, they were burdened by compulsion and force, not that they took it up willingly and by choice. Rather, they were like those under obligation who, when burdened, did not lift their heads with it.

Another: that when they were burdened with it by compulsion and force, they did not accept it, and did not carry it with contentment and choice, though they knew that they had no escape from carrying it, and that if they carried it by choice, it would bring them a good outcome in this world and the next.

Another: that it contains the interests of their livelihood, their return (to Allah), and their happiness in this world and the next, and their turning away from adhering to what brings them happiness and success, toward its opposite, is the utmost of ignorance, folly and lack of discernment.

Among their ignorance and their scant knowledge is that they sought, in exchange for manna and quails, which are among the finest, most wholesome and most suitable foods for good nourishment, the following: greens, cucumbers, garlic, lentils and onions. Whoever is content to exchange these foods for manna and quails should not find it surprising that he would exchange disbelief for faith, misguidance for guidance, wrath for pleasure, and punishment for mercy. This is the state of one who knows neither his Lord, nor His Book, nor His Messenger, nor himself.

Words correspond to the meanings they convey. He said to me, may God have mercy on him: "This often happens to me too. Consider the letter (la) (لا), how you find it: a lam followed by an alif, through which the voice is extended, as long as the breath does not cut it short. The extension of its sound indicates the extension of its meaning, and this will not be reversed. So reflect on it. It is a wonderful meaning. And look at how it comes in the most eloquent speech, the speech of God: ﴿And they will never wish for it, ever﴾, with the letter (la) in the place where the conditional particle is joined to the verb, so that it becomes one of the forms of generality, extending over all times. This is His saying, mighty and majestic: ﴿If you claim that you are God's allies to the exclusion of other people, then wish for death﴾. It is as if He says: whenever they claim that at any time or in any age, and they are told, 'Wish for death,' they will never wish for it, ever. The conditional particle indicates this meaning, and the letter la in the response corresponds to the form of generality, because of the breadth of the meaning of negation in it. In Surat al-Baqarah He said: ﴿and they will never wish for it﴾ (wa-lan yatamannawhu), with (lan), which reduces the breadth of negation and makes it closer, because before it is: ﴿Say: If the Last Abode with God is yours alone﴾. (In) and (kana) here are not forms of generality, because (kana) does not indicate an event; it is only attached to the subject, and its predicate expresses the passage of the time in which that event occurred. So it is as if He, mighty and majestic, says: if the Last Abode has been decreed for you and established for you in God's knowledge, then wish for death now. Then He said in the answer: ﴿and they will never wish for it﴾, so the meaning of the response matched the meaning of the address in both verses.

There is nothing in His saying "ever" (abadan) that contradicts what we have said, for "ever" may follow a present-tense verb, as you say: Zayd stands ever (yaqumu abadan)."

**(Benefit: The Names of the Days)**

Since the days are alike, with no day distinguished from another by an intrinsic or a conceptual attribute, the only way to tell them apart is by number. For this reason, the names of the days of the week were derived from numbers, such as *al-Ithnayn* (Monday, "the second"), *al-Thulathaa'* (Tuesday, "the third"), and *al-Arbi'aa'* (Wednesday, "the fourth"). They were also named after events that occurred on them, such as the Day of Bu'ath, the Day of Badr, and the Day of the Conquest (al-Fath). From this category is the name *Yawm al-Jumu'ah* (Friday).

Regarding it there are two opinions:

The first: it is so named because people gather (*ijtima'*) on it for prayer.

The second, which is the correct one: because it is the day on which creation was gathered and completed, and it is the day on which Allah will gather the first and the last for the judgment (*fasl al-qada'*).

As for Saturday (*Yawm al-Sabt*), it is derived from *al-qat'* (cutting off), as this root suggests, and from *al-sabat* (rest/torpor), because living beings cease movement and livelihood on it. The "sabtiyyah" sandals are those from which the hair has been cut off. The cause of *sabat* is an illness that cuts the sick person off from movement and speech. It was not one of the days of the creation of the world. Rather, the first of the days of creation was Sunday (*al-Ahad*), and its last was Friday. This is the more correct of the two opinions, and it is what the Qur'an indicates, and the consensus of the Muslim community holds that the days of the creation of the world were six. Had the first of them been Saturday, they would have been seven.

As for the hadith of Abu Hurayrah narrated by Muslim in his Sahih:

"Allah created the clay on Saturday."

(Narrated by Muslim.)

al-Bukhari mentioned in his *Tarikh* that it is a defective hadith (*mu'allal*), and that the correct version is that it is a statement of Ka'b (al-Ahbar).

This is as he stated, because it implies that the days of creation were seven, and the Qur'an rejects this.

Know that knowledge of the days of the week is not attained through the senses, nor through reason, nor through any convention by which the week is distinguished from other periods. It is known only through revelation (*al-shar'*). For this reason, only the people of the revealed religions, and those who received this knowledge from them and lived among them, know the days of the week.

As for the nations that do not adhere to any religion or scripture, the week is not distinguished from other periods among them, and its days are not distinguished from one another. This differs from the knowledge of the month and the year, which is based on what can be observed.

**(Subtle Point)**

His saying in the hadith about Friday: "and the pages are folded up" means the pages of merit (*suhuf al-fadl*). As for the pages of obligation (*suhuf al-fard*), they are not folded up, because the obligation falls away after that.

**[Chapter on his guidance ﷺ regarding Friday and mention of the distinctive features of its day]**

It is established in the *Sahihayn* from the Prophet ﷺ that he said:

"We are the last (in time) and the first (in precedence) on the Day of Resurrection, though they were given the Book before us. Then this is their day which Allah made obligatory upon them, but they differed about it, so Allah guided us to it. People are following us in it: the Jews tomorrow and the Christians the day after tomorrow."

In *Sahih Muslim*, from Abu Hurayrah and Hudhayfah, may Allah be pleased with them both, they both said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Allah led astray from Friday those who were before us. The Jews had Saturday, and the Christians had Sunday. Then Allah brought us and guided us to Friday, so He made Friday, Saturday and Sunday (in that order). Likewise they are following us on the Day of Resurrection. We are the last of the people of this world and the first on the Day of Resurrection, to whom judgment will be decided before all the creatures."

In the *Musnad* and the *Sunan*, from the hadith of Aws ibn Aws, from the Prophet ﷺ:

"Among your best days is Friday. On it Allah created Adam, on it he died, on it is the blowing of the trumpet, and on it is the swoon. So send abundant blessings upon me on it, for your blessings are presented to me." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, how will our blessings be presented to you when you have decayed?" (meaning: you have become worn away). He said: "Allah has forbidden the earth to consume the bodies of the prophets."

It was narrated by al-Hakim in the *Mustadrak* and by Ibn Hibban in his *Sahih*.

In the *Jami' al-Tirmidhi*, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "The best day on which the sun has risen is Friday. On it Allah created Adam, on it he was admitted into Paradise, and on it he was expelled from it. The Hour will not come except on a Friday." He said: "A good, sound hadith," and al-Hakim authenticated it.

Also in the *Mustadrak*, from Abu Hurayrah, raised to the Prophet: "The lord of the days is Friday. On it Adam was created, on it he was admitted into Paradise, on it he was expelled from it, and the Hour will not come except on a Friday."

Malik narrated in the *Muwatta'*, from Abu Hurayrah, raised to the Prophet: "The best day on which the sun has risen is Friday. On it Adam was created, on it he was sent down, on it he was forgiven, on it he died, and on it the Hour will come. There is no creature that is not attentive (*musikhah*) on Friday from the morning until sunrise, out of fear of the Hour, except the jinn and mankind. And on it there is an hour in which no Muslim servant who is praying and asks Allah for something will fail to be given it." Ka'b said: "That is one day in every year." I said: "Rather, it is in every week." Then Ka'b read the Torah and said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ spoke the truth." Abu Hurayrah said: "Then I met Abdullah ibn Salam and told him about my session with Ka'b." He said: "I know which hour it is." I said: "Then tell me about it." He said: "It is the last hour of Friday." I said: "How can it be, when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'No Muslim servant who is praying will encounter it,' and that hour is not one in which prayer is performed?" Ibn Salam said: "Did not the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'Whoever sits in a place waiting for the prayer is in prayer until he prays'?"

In *Sahih Ibn Hibban*, raised to the Prophet: "The sun has not risen on a day better than Friday."

In the *Musnad al-Shafi'i*, from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, who said:

"Jibril (peace be upon him) came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with a white mirror in which there was a speck. The Prophet ﷺ said: 'What is this?' He said: 'This is Friday, which you and your community have been favored with. People follow you in it: the Jews and the Christians. For you there is good in it, and in it there is an hour in which no believing servant who calls upon Allah for something good will meet it without being answered. And it is with us the Day of Increase (*yawm al-mazid*).' The Prophet ﷺ said: 'O Jibril, what is the Day of Increase?' He said: 'Your Lord has taken in Paradise a wide valley in which there are mounds of musk. When it is Friday, Allah, glorified is He, sends down whatever of His angels He wills, and around Him are pulpits of light on which sit the prophets, and those pulpits are surrounded by pulpits of gold adorned with rubies and chrysolite, on which sit the martyrs and the truthful (*siddiqun*), and they sit behind them on those mounds.' Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: 'I am your Lord. I have fulfilled My promise to you. Ask Me and I will give you.' They say: 'Our Lord, we ask You for Your good pleasure.' He says: 'I am pleased with you, and for you is what you wished, and with Me is more.' So they love Friday because of the good that their Lord gives them on it. It is the day on which your Lord, blessed and exalted, rose over the Throne, on it Adam was created, and on it the Hour will come.'"

It was narrated by al-Shafi'i from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad, who said: Musa ibn Ubaydah told me, who said: Abu al-Azhar Mu'awiyah ibn Ishaq ibn Talhah told me, from Abdullah ibn Ubayd, from Umayr ibn Anas.

Then he said: Ibrahim informed us, who said: Abu Imran Ibrahim ibn al-Ja'd told me, from Anas, something similar to it.

Al-Shafi'i had a good opinion of his teacher Ibrahim, but Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, said of him: "A Mu'tazili, Jahmi, Qadari; every calamity is in him."

Abu al-Yaman al-Hakam ibn Nafi' narrated it: Safwan told us, who said: Anas said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Jibril came to me and mentioned it..." It was also narrated by Muhammad ibn Shu'ayb from Umar, the client of Ghafrah, from Anas. It was also narrated by Abu Dhabyah from Uthman ibn Umayr, from Anas. Abu Bakr ibn Abi Dawud collected its chains of transmission.

In the *Musnad of Ahmad*, from the hadith of Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: "It was said to the Prophet ﷺ: 'Why is Friday called so?' He said: 'Because on it the clay of your father Adam was molded, on it is the swoon and the resurrection, on it is the seizing (*al-bat'ah*), and at its end are three hours, one of which is an hour in which whoever calls upon Allah will be answered.'"

Al-Hasan ibn Sufyan al-Nasawi said in his *Musnad*: Abu Marwan Hisham ibn Khalid al-Azraq told us, who said: al-Hasan ibn Yahya al-Khushani told us, who said: Umar ibn Abdullah, the client of Ghafrah, told us, who said: Anas ibn Malik told me, who said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'Jibril came to me holding something like a white mirror, in which there was a black speck. I said: What is this, O Jibril? He said: This is Friday, which I was sent to you with, to be a festival for you and your community after you. I said: What is there for us in it, O Jibril? He said: For you in it is much good. You are the last and the first on the Day of Resurrection. In it there is an hour in which no Muslim servant who is praying and asks Allah for something will fail to be given it. I said: What is this black speck, O Jibril? He said: This is the hour which occurs on Friday, and it is the lord of the days, and we call it with us the Day of Increase. I said: What is the Day of Increase, O Jibril? He said: That is because your Lord has taken in Paradise a wide valley of white musk. When it is a day of Friday of the days of the Hereafter, the Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, descends from His Throne to His Footstool (*kursi*). The Footstool is surrounded by pulpits of light, on which the prophets sit. The pulpits are surrounded by chairs of gold, on which the truthful and the martyrs sit. The people of the chambers (*ahl al-ghuraf*) descend from their chambers and sit on mounds of musk; they see no superiority of the people of the pulpits and chairs in the assembly. Then the Possessor of Majesty and Honor, blessed and exalted, appears to them and says: "Ask Me." They all say: "We ask You for Your good pleasure, O Lord." He bears witness to their good pleasure. Then He says: "Ask Me," and they ask Him until the desire of each one of them is fulfilled. Then there will be brought to them what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and what has not occurred to the heart of any human. Then the Almighty rises from His Footstool to His Throne, and the people of the chambers rise to their chambers, which are a chamber of white pearl, or red ruby, or green emerald, without any crack or flaw, illuminated, with its rivers flowing or, he said, running, its fruits hanging down, and in it are their spouses, their servants, and their dwellings.'

He said: 'The people of Paradise rejoice in Paradise on the Day of Friday, just as the people of this world rejoice in this world at the rain.'"

Ibn Abi al-Dunya said in the book *Sifat al-Jannah* (The Description of Paradise): Azhar ibn Marwan al-Raqashi told me, who said: Abdullah ibn Aradah al-Shaybani told me, who said: al-Qasim ibn Mutayyib told us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Wa'il, from Hudhayfah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 62, verses 9–10 (part 2 of 6):

"Jibril came to me holding in his palm a mirror, the most beautiful and brightest of mirrors, and in its center was a black spot. I said: 'What is this spot that I see in it?' He said: 'This is al-Jumu'ah.' I said: 'And what is al-Jumu'ah?' He said: 'It is a great day among the days of your Lord. I will inform you of its nobility and virtue in this world, what is hoped for in it by its people, and I will inform you of its name in the Hereafter. As for its nobility and virtue in this world, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has gathered in it the affairs of creation. As for what is hoped for in it by its people, there is in it an hour that no Muslim servant or Muslim woman will coincide with while asking Allah, Exalted, for good, except that He gives it to them.' As for its nobility, its virtue and its name in the Hereafter, when Allah, Blessed and Exalted, brings the people of Paradise into Paradise and the people of the Fire into the Fire, these days and nights will pass over them, with no night or day in them except that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knows its measure and its hours. When the day of Jumu'ah comes, when the people of Jumu'ah go out to their congregation, a caller will call out to the people of Paradise: 'O people of Paradise! Go out to the Valley of Increase (Wadi al-Mazid).' The Valley of Increase, its length and breadth are known only to Allah. In it are dunes of musk whose tops rise into the sky.' He said: 'The youths of the Prophets will come out on pulpits of light, and the youths of the believers will come out on thrones of ruby. When these are placed for them and the people take their seats, Allah will send upon them a wind called al-Muthirah, which stirs up that musk, carries it under their garments and brings it out onto their faces and hair. That wind knows better how to treat that musk than the wife of any one of you would, even if every perfume on the face of the earth were given to her.' He said: 'Then Allah, Blessed and Exalted, will reveal to the bearers of His Throne: Place it among them. The first thing they will hear from it will be: Come to Me, O My servants who obeyed Me unseen, who did not see Me, who believed in My messengers and followed My command. Ask Me, for this is the Day of Increase.' They will gather upon one word: 'We are pleased with You, so be pleased with us.' Then Allah will reply to them: 'O people of Paradise, if I were not pleased with you, I would not have made you dwell in My abode. Ask Me, for this is the Day of Increase.' They will gather upon one word: 'Our Lord, we wish to look upon Your Face.' Then He will lift those veils, and Mighty and Majestic will manifest Himself to them. There will envelop them of His light something which, were it not that He had decreed they should not be burned, would burn them because of what envelops them of His light. Then it will be said to them: 'Return to your abodes.' They will return to their abodes, having been given double of what they had. They will return to their wives, who will find them changed and they will find the wives changed by what has enveloped them of His light. When they return, the light will recede until they return to the forms they had been upon. Their wives will say to them: 'You went out from our presence in one form and you have returned in another.' They will say: 'That is because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, manifested Himself to us, and we looked upon Him.'" He said: "By Allah, no creation has encompassed Him, but He showed them of His greatness and majesty what He willed to show them." He said: "That is their saying: 'and we looked upon Him.'" He said: "They will then turn about in the musk and bliss of Paradise, every seven days, double of what they had been in."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "That is His saying, Exalted: ﴿No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for the eyes, as a reward for what they used to do﴾ [As-Sajdah: 17]."

Abu Nu'aym narrated it in *Sifat al-Jannah* from the hadith of 'Ismah ibn Muhammad, from Musa ibn 'Uqbah, from Abu Salih, from Anas, similar to it.

Abu Nu'aym also mentioned in *Sifat al-Jannah*, from the hadith of al-Mas'udi, from al-Minhal, from Abu 'Ubaydah, from 'Abdullah, who said:

"Hasten to the Jumu'ah in this world, for Allah, Blessed and Exalted, appears to the people of Paradise every Friday upon a mound of white camphor, and they will be near Him, Glorified, according to the speed with which they hastened to the Jumu'ah. He will bring for them, from honour, something they had not seen before, and they will return to their families, and it will have been renewed for them."

[Section on the origin of Jumu'ah]

Ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Abi Umamah ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf narrated to me, from his father, who said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ka'b ibn Malik narrated to me, saying: "I was the guide of my father when his sight failed. When I took him out to the Jumu'ah and he heard the adhan (call to prayer) for it, he would seek forgiveness for Abu Umamah As'ad ibn Zurarah. He persisted in this for a while, so I said: 'This is weakness; should I not ask him about this?' So I took him out as I used to, and when he heard the adhan for the Jumu'ah, he sought forgiveness for him. I said: 'O father! Do you see your seeking forgiveness for As'ad ibn Zurarah whenever you hear the adhan on Friday?' He said: 'O my son! As'ad was the first who gathered us for Friday prayer in Madinah, before the arrival of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), at Hazm al-Nabit in the lava field of Banu Bayadah, in a pool called Naqi' al-Khadamat.' I said: 'How many were you that day?' He said: 'Forty men.'"

Al-Bayhaqi said: "Muhammad ibn Ishaq, when his hearing from the narrator is mentioned, and the narrator is trustworthy, the chain is sound. This is a good hadith with a sound chain." End of quotation.

I say: This was the beginning of the Jumu'ah. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to Madinah, and he stayed at Quba among Banu 'Amr ibn 'Awf, as Ibn Ishaq said, on Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday, and he founded their mosque. Then he went out on Friday and the Jumu'ah overtook him among Banu Salim ibn 'Awf, and he prayed it in the mosque that is in the bottom of the valley. It was the first Jumu'ah he prayed in Madinah, and that was before the founding of his mosque.

Ibn Ishaq said: "The first khutbah (sermon) that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) delivered, as it has reached me, was from Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, and we seek refuge in Allah from saying about the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) what he did not say, that he stood among them delivering a sermon, praised Allah and extolled Him with what is due to Him, then said: 'Amma ba'd. O people, send ahead for your souls. You will know, by Allah, one of you will be struck senseless, then will leave his sheep with no shepherd. Then his Lord will say to him, with no interpreter and no chamberlain to veil him from Him: Did My messenger not come to you and convey to you? I gave you wealth and bestowed favours upon you. What did you send ahead for yourself? Then he will look to his right and to his left and see nothing. Then he will look before him and see nothing but Hellfire. Whoever is able to shield his face from the Fire, even with half a date, let him do so; and whoever does not find it, then with a good word, for by it a good deed is rewarded tenfold up to seven hundredfold. Peace be upon you, and the mercy and blessings of Allah.'"

Ibn Ishaq said: "Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) delivered a sermon another time, saying: 'Indeed all praise is for Allah. We praise Him and seek His help. We seek refuge in Allah from the evils of our souls and the bad consequences of our deeds. Whomever Allah guides, none can misguide; and whomever He misguides, none can guide. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, alone, without partner. Indeed the best speech is the Book of Allah. Prosperous is he whom Allah has adorned in his heart, and has brought into Islam after disbelief, so that he prefers it over other human talk. It is the best and most eloquent speech. Love what Allah loves. Love Allah with all your hearts. Do not tire of the words of Allah and His remembrance, and do not let your hearts harden against it, for of all that Allah creates He chooses and selects. He has named it His choice among deeds, His chosen among servants, and the righteous speech, and of all that people are given of what is lawful and unlawful. So worship Allah and do not associate anything with Him. Fear Him as He should be feared, and be truthful to Allah in what you say with your mouths. Love one another with the Spirit of Allah among you. Indeed Allah is angered when His covenant is broken. Peace be upon you, and the mercy and blessings of Allah.'"

A portion of his sermon (peace be upon him) has already been mentioned when discussing his guidance in sermons.

[Section on the special features of the Day of Jumu'ah, which are thirty-three]

It was part of the guidance of the Prophet (ﷺ) to honour this day and exalt it, and to single it out with acts of worship that are specific to it apart from other days.

The scholars have differed as to whether it is better, or the Day of 'Arafah. There are two opinions, which are two views of the companions of al-Shafi'i.

The Prophet (ﷺ) used to recite in the dawn prayer on it the two surahs *Alif-Lam-Mim Tanzil* and *Hal Ata 'ala al-Insan*.

Many who have no knowledge suppose that the purpose is to single out this prayer with an additional prostration, and they call it the Sajdah of Jumu'ah. When one of them does not recite this surah, he considers it recommended to recite another surah that contains a prostration. For this reason, some of the imams disliked continual recitation of this surah at the Friday dawn prayer, to prevent the misconception of the ignorant. I heard Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah say: The Prophet (ﷺ) only recited these two surahs at the Friday dawn prayer because they contain what has happened and what will happen on its day. They encompass the creation of Adam, the mention of the Return and the gathering of servants, and that occurs on the Day of Jumu'ah. Reciting them on this day is a reminder to the Ummah of what was and what will be. The prostration came incidentally, not intended, so that the worshipper does not intend to recite it wherever it happens to occur.

This is one of the special features of the Day of Jumu'ah.

The second special feature is the recommendation of increasing prayers upon the Prophet (ﷺ) on it and on its night, based on his saying (ﷺ): "Increase your prayers upon me on the Day of Jumu'ah and the Night of Jumu'ah."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is the master of mankind, and the Day of Jumu'ah is the master of days. So there is a distinction in sending prayers upon him on this day that is not found for anything else, along with another wisdom: every good that his Ummah attains in this world and the Hereafter, it attains through him. Allah has combined for his Ummah through him the two good things of this world and the Hereafter. The greatest honour that they receive comes on the Day of Jumu'ah, for on it they are raised to their homes and palaces in Paradise. It is the Day of Increase for them when they enter Paradise. It is their day of festival in this world, a day on which Allah, Exalted, grants them their requests and needs, and He does not turn away their petitioners. All this they came to know and obtained through him and by means of him. So from thanking him, praising him and fulfilling a little of his right (ﷺ) is that we increase our prayers upon him on this day and its night.

The third special feature: the Friday prayer (Salat al-Jumu'ah), which is among the most emphasized obligations of Islam and among the greatest assemblies of the Muslims. It is greater than every gathering they convene and more obligatory than it, apart from the gathering at 'Arafah. Whoever abandons it out of negligence, Allah will seal his heart, bring near the people of Paradise on the Day of Resurrection, and they will precede him to the visit on the Day of Increase according to their nearness to the imam on Friday and their earliness.

The fourth special feature is the command to perform ghusl (ritual bath) on its day, which is a very strongly emphasized matter. Its obligation is stronger than the obligation of the witr prayer, of reciting the basmalah in the prayer, of wudu' from touching women, of wudu' from touching the private part, of wudu' from laughing aloud in prayer, of wudu' from nosebleed, from cupping and from vomiting, and of sending prayers upon the Prophet (ﷺ) in the final tashahhud, and of reciting behind the imam for the follower.

There are three opinions among the people regarding its obligation: negation, affirmation, and a distinction between one who has an odour that requires removal, for whom it is obligatory, and one who is free of it, for whom it is recommended. These three are the views of the companions of Ahmad.

The fifth special feature: perfuming oneself on it, which is better than perfuming on the other days of the week.

The sixth special feature: using the siwak (tooth-stick) on it, which has a distinction over siwak on other days.

The seventh special feature: early arrival for the prayer.

The eighth special feature: occupying oneself with prayer, remembrance and recitation until the imam comes out.

The ninth special feature: listening attentively to the khutbah when one hears it, which is obligatory according to the more correct of the two opinions. If one neglects it, he has engaged in idle talk, and whoever engages in idle talk has no Jumu'ah. In the *Musnad* it is narrated as a marfu' hadith: "And whoever says to his companion, 'Be quiet,' has no Jumu'ah."

The tenth special feature: reciting Surat al-Kahf on its day. It has been narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever recites Surat al-Kahf on the Day of Jumu'ah, a light will shine for him from beneath his foot up to the clouds of the sky, illuminating him on the Day of Resurrection, and his sins between the two Fridays will be forgiven."

Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated it as a saying of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, and this is more likely.

Eleventh: Performing prayer during this day at the time of zawal (the sun's decline after its zenith) is not disliked, according to al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, and whoever agrees with him. This is the view chosen by our shaykh Abu al-'Abbas Ibn Taymiyyah. His reliance was not on the hadith of Layth from Mujahid from Abu al-Khalil from Abu Qatadah from the Prophet ﷺ, that "he disliked prayer at midday except on Friday."

And [the hadith] that says: "Indeed Hell is kindled except on Friday." Rather, his reliance was on the fact that whoever comes to the Friday prayer is recommended to pray until the imam comes out. In the authentic hadith: "No man bathes on Friday and purifies himself as much as he can, anoints himself with his oil, or applies perfume from his house, then goes out and does not separate two people, then prays what has been written for him, then remains silent when the imam speaks, except that he is forgiven for what is between him and the next Friday." Narrated by al-Bukhari. So he (the Prophet ﷺ) urged prayer as much as had been written for him, and he prevented him from it only at the time the imam comes out. For this reason, more than one of the early scholars, among them 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, and Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, who followed him in this, said: "The imam's coming out prevents prayer, and his khutbah prevents speech." Thus they made the impediment to prayer the imam's coming out, not the midpoint of the day.

Also, people are in the mosque under roofs and do not perceive the time of zawal, and a man may be occupied with prayer without knowing the time of zawal; he cannot go out, step over people's necks, look at the sun, and return, and this is not prescribed for him.

As for this hadith of Abu Qatadah, Abu Dawud said: it is mursal, because Abu al-Khalil did not hear from Abu Qatadah. A mursal hadith, when it is connected [by other chains], is acted upon, and it is strengthened by analogy, or the statement of a companion, or when its narrator (in the mursal) is known for choosing the shaykhs and avoiding narration from the weak and the abandoned and the like, which indicates its strength; then it is acted upon.

Also, it is strengthened by other corroborating reports, among them what al-Shafi'i mentioned in his book, saying: It is related from Ishaq ibn 'Abd Allah, from Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id, from Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet ﷺ "forbade prayer at midday until the sun declines, except on Friday."

Thus he related it, may Allah have mercy on him, in the book "Ikhtilaf al-Hadith," and he related it in the "Kitab al-Jumu'ah": "Ibrahim ibn Muhammad narrated to us from Ishaq." Abu Khalid al-Ahmar related it from a shaykh from the people of Madinah called 'Abd Allah ibn Sa'id al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ. Al-Bayhaqi related it in "al-Ma'rifah" from the hadith of 'Ata' ibn 'Ajlan from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id and Abu Hurayrah, who said: "The Prophet ﷺ used to forbid prayer at midday except on Friday." But in its chain there is someone who is not relied upon as evidence, as al-Bayhaqi said. He said: But when these hadiths are combined with the hadith of Abu Qatadah, they generate some strength.

Al-Shafi'i said: It is the custom of people to hasten to the Friday prayer and to pray until the imam comes out. Al-Bayhaqi said: What al-Shafi'i indicated is present in the authentic hadiths, namely that the Prophet ﷺ encouraged hastening to the Friday prayer and praying until the imam comes out without exception, and this agrees with these hadiths in which prayer at midday on Friday is permitted. We have also related the concession in this matter from 'Ata', Tawus, al-Hasan and Makhul.

I say: People have differed about the disliking of prayer at midday on three views. The first: that it is not a time of dislike at all, and this is the position of Malik. The second: that it is a time of dislike on Friday and other days, and this is the position of Abu Hanifah, and the well-known position of Ahmad. The third: that it is a time of dislike except on Friday; on Friday it is not a time of dislike, and this is the position of al-Shafi'i.

Twelfth: Reciting (Surat al-Jumu'ah) and (al-Munafiqun), or (Sabbih) and al-Ghashiyah, in the Friday prayer. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to recite these in the Friday prayer, as Muslim mentioned in his "Sahih."

Also in it: that he ﷺ used to recite in it (al-Jumu'ah) and ﴿Has there come to you the report of the overwhelming?﴾ All of this is established from him.

It is not recommended to recite part of each surah, or to recite one of them in the two rak'ahs, for this is contrary to the Sunnah, and ignorant leaders persist in doing so.

Thirteenth: It is a day of recurring festival in the week. Abu 'Abd Allah Ibn Majah related in his "Sunan," from the hadith of Abu Lubabah ibn 'Abd al-Mundhir, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Indeed the day of Friday is the lord of days, and the greatest of them before Allah, and it is greater before Allah than the day of al-Adha and the day of al-Fitr. In it are five qualities: Allah created Adam in it, and Allah sent Adam down to the earth in it, and Allah caused Adam to die in it, and in it there is an hour in which the servant asks Allah for nothing except that He gives it to him, so long as he does not ask for something unlawful, and in it the Hour will be established. There is no angel brought near, nor heaven, nor earth, nor winds, nor mountains, nor trees, except that they are apprehensive of the day of Friday."

Fourteenth: It is recommended to wear the best clothing one is able to afford on it. Imam Ahmad related in his "Musnad" from the hadith of Abu Ayyub, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:

"Whoever bathes on Friday, and applies perfume if he has any, and wears the best of his clothes, then goes out with tranquility until he comes to the mosque, then prays what he wishes to pray, and does not harm anyone, then listens attentively when his imam comes out until he prays, it will be an expiation for what is between them."

And in "Sunan Abi Dawud," from 'Abd Allah ibn Salam, that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say on the minbar on Friday: "What is upon one of you if he buys two garments for Friday, apart from his two garments of work?"

And in "Sunan Ibn Majah," from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that the Prophet ﷺ addressed the people on Friday and saw on them garments of wool, and said: "What is upon one of you if he finds means to take two garments for his Friday, apart from his two garments of work?"

Fifteenth: It is recommended on it to perfume the mosque with incense. Sa'id ibn Mansur mentioned, from Nu'aym ibn 'Abd Allah al-Mujmir, that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, ordered that the mosque of Madinah be perfumed every Friday when midday arrives.

I say: For this reason Nu'aym was called al-Mujmir.

Sixteenth: It is not permitted to travel on its day for one obligated to attend the Friday prayer, after it has become obligatory by entry of its time. As for before it, there are three views among the scholars, and they are explicit reports from Ahmad: one, it is not permitted; two, it is permitted; three, it is permitted only for jihad specifically.

As for the position of al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, it is prohibited in his view to begin travel on Friday after zawal. Among them, regarding travel for obedience, there are two aspects: one, its prohibition, which is the choice of al-Nawawi; the second, its permissibility, which is the choice of al-Rafi'i.

As for travel before zawal, al-Shafi'i has two views: the old view, its permissibility; and the new view, that it is like travel after zawal.

As for the position of Malik, the author of "al-Tafri'" said: No one should travel on Friday after zawal until he has prayed the Friday prayer. There is no harm in traveling before zawal, and the preferred course is that one who is present should not travel when dawn has risen until he has prayed the Friday prayer.

Abu Hanifah went to the permissibility of travel absolutely. Al-Daraqutni related in "al-Afrad" from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Whoever travels from his dwelling-place on Friday, the angels invoke against him that he not be accompanied on his journey."

And this is from the hadith of Ibn Lahi'ah.

And in "Musnad Imam Ahmad," from the hadith of al-Hakam from Miqsam from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent 'Abd Allah ibn Rawahah in a military expedition, and it happened to be a Friday. He said: his companions set out in the morning, and he said: I will stay behind and pray with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then I will catch up with them. When the Prophet ﷺ prayed, he saw him and said: What prevented you from setting out with your companions? He said: I wanted to pray with you, then catch up with them. He said: 'Even if you spent what is on the earth, you would not attain the virtue of their morning departure.'"

This hadith has been criticized on the ground that al-Hakam did not hear from Miqsam.

This applies when the traveler does not fear missing his company. If he fears missing his company and being cut off after them, it is permitted for him to travel absolutely, because this is an excuse that drops the Friday and congregational prayer.

Perhaps what is related from al-Awza'i, that he was asked about a traveler who heard the Friday call to prayer while he had already saddled his mount, and he said: let him proceed on his journey, is to be understood in this way. Likewise the statement of Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him: "The Friday does not detain one from travel."

If their intention was the permissibility of travel absolutely, then it is a matter of dispute. The proof is decisive against it: 'Abd al-Razzaq related in his "Musannaf" from Ma'mar from Khalid al-Hadhdha' from Ibn Sirin or others, that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab saw a man wearing travel clothes after he had finished the Friday prayer, and said: What is your matter? He said: I wanted to travel, but I disliked to leave until I had prayed. 'Umar said: "The Friday does not prevent you from travel so long as its time has not come." This is the view of one who prohibits travel after zawal and does not prohibit it before it.

'Abd al-Razzaq also mentioned it from al-Thawri from al-Aswad ibn Qays, from his father, who said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab saw a man with the appearance of a traveler, and the man said: Today is Friday, and were it not for that I would have set out. 'Umar said: "The Friday does not detain a traveler, so set out so long as the time of departure (al-rawah) has not come."

He also mentioned from al-Thawri, from Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from Salih ibn Kathir, from al-Zuhri, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out as a traveler on Friday in the forenoon before the prayer."

He mentioned from Ma'mar, who said: I asked Yahya ibn Abi Kathir: Does a man go out on Friday? He disliked it, so I began to narrate to him the concession regarding it. He said to me: Rarely does a man go out on Friday without seeing what he dislikes; if you look into it, you will find it so.

Ibn al-Mubarak mentioned from al-Awza'i, from Hassan ibn Abi 'Atiyyah, who said: If a man travels on Friday, the day invokes against him that he not be helped in his need and not be accompanied on his journey.

Al-Awza'i mentioned from Ibn al-Musayyab that he said: Travel on Friday is after the prayer. Ibn Jurayj said: I said to 'Ata': Has it reached you that it used to be said: if one reaches the night of Friday in a populated town, he should not leave until he has gathered for the Friday prayer? He said: That indeed is disliked.

I said: And from Thursday? He said: No, that day is not harmful to him.

Seventeenth: For one walking to the Friday prayer, each step carries the reward of a year's fasting and standing in prayer. 'Abd al-Razzaq said: from Ma'mar, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Qilabah, from Abu al-Ash'ath al-San'ani, from Aws ibn Aws, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever washes [his wife] and bathes on Friday, and hastens early and comes early, and draws near to the imam and listens attentively, for him there is with every step he takes the reward of a year's fasting and standing [in prayer], and that is easy for Allah." Imam Ahmad related it in his "Musnad."

Imam Ahmad said: "ghassala" with the doubled letter means he had intercourse with his wife; and Waki' interpreted it thus.

Eighteenth: It is the day of the expiation of sins. Imam Ahmad related in his "Musnad" from Salman, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: "Do you know what the day of Friday is?"

I said: It is the day on which Allah gathered your father Adam. He said: "But I know what the day of Friday is. A man does not purify himself and perfect his purification, then comes to the Friday prayer and listens attentively until the imam finishes his prayer, except that it becomes an expiation for what is between it and the coming Friday, so long as the great sins are avoided."

And in the "Musnad" also, from the hadith of 'Ata' al-Khurasani, from Nubaishah al-Hudhali, that he used to narrate from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Indeed, when a Muslim bathes on Friday, then comes to the mosque without harming anyone, if he does not find the imam, he goes out, prays what he wishes; and if he finds the imam has already come out, he sits, listens and remains silent until the imam finishes his Friday prayer and his speech. If his sins are not all forgiven in that Friday, they will be an expiation for the Friday that follows it."

In the *Sahih al-Bukhari* (the "Sound" collection of al-Bukhari), on the authority of Salman, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

"No man bathes on the day of Jumu'ah (Friday) and purifies himself as much as he can, anoints himself with his oil or applies some perfume from his household, then goes out and does not separate two people (by pushing between them), then prays what has been decreed for him, then listens attentively when the imam speaks, except that his sins between this Jumu'ah and the next will be forgiven."

In the *Musnad of Ahmad* (Ahmad ibn Hanbal's collection of narrations arranged by companion), from the hadith of Abu al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

"Whoever bathes on the day of Jumu'ah, then puts on his clothes, and applies perfume if he has any, then walks to the Jumu'ah with tranquility, does not step over anyone, does not harm anyone, prays what has been prescribed for him, then waits until the imam finishes, his sins between the two Jumu'ahs will be forgiven."

**Nineteenth:** That Jahannam (Hell) is kindled every day except the day of Jumu'ah. The hadith of Abu Qatadah on this has already been mentioned. The secret of this, and Allah knows best, is that it is the best of days in the sight of Allah, and in it occur acts of obedience, worship, supplications, and humble pleading to Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, which prevent Hell from being kindled on it. For this reason the sins of the believers on it are fewer than their sins on other days, to the extent that the wicked refrain on it from what they do not refrain from on Saturday and other days.

This hadith apparently means the kindling of Hell in this world, that it is fired every day except the day of Jumu'ah. As for the Day of Resurrection, its punishment does not abate, and it is not lightened for its people, who are its inhabitants, for a single day. For this reason they will call upon the guardians (of Hell) to ask their Lord to lighten the punishment for them for one day, and they will not be answered in that.

**Twentieth:** That in it is the hour of response, the hour in which no Muslim servant asks Allah for anything except that He gives it to him. In the *Sahihayn* (the two *Sahih* collections of al-Bukhari and Muslim), from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

"Indeed on Friday there is an hour in which no Muslim servant, standing in prayer, asks Allah for anything except that He gives it to him." And he gestured with his hand, indicating how brief it is.

In the *Musnad*, from the hadith of Abu Lubabah ibn Abd al-Mundhir, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said:

"The master of days is the day of Jumu'ah, and it is the greatest of days in the sight of Allah, and greater in the sight of Allah than the day of Fitr (Eid al-Fitr) and the day of Adha (Eid al-Adha). In it are five characteristics: Allah created Adam on it, Allah sent Adam down to the earth on it, Allah took Adam's soul on it, there is an hour in it in which no servant asks Allah for anything except that Allah gives him what he asks, as long as he does not ask for something unlawful, and the Hour will be established on it. There is no angel brought near, nor earth, nor winds, nor sea, nor mountains, nor trees, except that they are apprehensive of the day of Jumu'ah."

[Section on the disagreement of people concerning the hour of response]

People have differed concerning this hour: is it still in existence, or has it been lifted?

There are two opinions, reported by Ibn Abd al-Barr and others. Those who said it still exists and has not been lifted disagreed as to whether it is at a specific time of the day or is not specified, on two views.

Then those who said it is not specified disagreed as to whether it moves through the hours of the day or not, on two views as well. Those who said it is specified disagreed on eleven opinions.

Ibn al-Mundhir said: It has been related to us from Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: It is from the rising of dawn until the rising of the sun, and after the Asr prayer until the setting of the sun.

The second: That it is at midday (zawal), mentioned by Ibn al-Mundhir from al-Hasan al-Basri and Abu al-Aliyah.

The third: That it is when the caller to prayer calls to the Jumu'ah prayer. Ibn al-Mundhir said: This has been related to us from Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her.

The fourth: That it is when the imam sits on the pulpit to deliver the khutbah (sermon) until he finishes. Ibn al-Mundhir said: It has been related to us from al-Hasan al-Basri.

The fifth: Said by Abu Burdah: It is the hour that Allah chose for the prayer.

The sixth: Said by Abu al-Sawwar al-Adawi, who said: They used to hold that supplication is answered between the decline of the sun and the time the prayer begins.

The seventh: Said by Abu Dharr: It is between the sun rising a span (shibr) and a cubit (dhira').

The eighth: That it is between Asr and the setting of the sun. Said by Abu Hurairah, Ata', Abdullah ibn Salam and Tawus. Ibn al-Mundhir related all of this.

The ninth: That it is the last hour after Asr. This is the view of Ahmad and the majority of the Companions and the Successors.

The tenth: That it is from the time the imam comes out until the end of the prayer. Related by al-Nawawi and others.

The eleventh: That it is the third hour of the day. Related by the author of *al-Mughni* on this matter.

Ka'b said: If a person divided a Friday among several Fridays, he would reach that hour.

Umar said: Indeed, seeking a need on a day is easy (i.e., one may find it on any day).

The most preponderant of these opinions are two, both supported by established hadiths, and one of them is more preponderant than the other.

The first: That it is from the sitting of the imam until the conclusion of the prayer. The evidence for this view is what Muslim related in his *Sahih* from the hadith of Abu Burdah ibn Abi Musa, that Abdullah ibn Umar said to him: "Did you hear your father narrate from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) anything about the hour of Jumu'ah?" He said: "Yes, I heard him say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'It is between when the imam sits and when the prayer is concluded.'"

Ibn Majah and al-Tirmidhi related from the hadith of Amr ibn Awf al-Muzani, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed on Jumu'ah there is an hour in which no servant asks Allah for anything except that Allah gives it to him." They said: "O Messenger of Allah! Which hour is it?" He said: "From when the prayer is established until one departs from it."

The second opinion: That it is after Asr, and this is the more preponderant of the two views. It is the view of Abdullah ibn Salam, Abu Hurairah, Imam Ahmad and a multitude (of scholars). The evidence for this view is what Ahmad related in his *Musnad* from the hadith of Abu Sa'id and Abu Hurairah that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed on Jumu'ah there is an hour in which no Muslim servant who asks Allah for good in it will fail to be given it, and it is after Asr."

Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i related from Jabir, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The day of Jumu'ah has twelve hours, in which there is an hour that no Muslim will find while asking Allah for something except that He gives it to him. So seek it in the last hour after Asr."

(Section)

The jurists have differed concerning this hour on two views:

One: That it is from the beginning of the day, and this is the known position in the school of al-Shafi'i, Ahmad and others.

The second: That it is part of the sixth hour after midday (zawal), and this is the known position in the school of Malik, and some Shafi'is chose it.

**Twenty-fifth:** That charity on it has a distinction over it on other days, and charity on it compared to the other days of the week is like charity in the month of Ramadan compared to the other months.

I witnessed Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah sanctify his soul, when he went out to the Jumu'ah, he would take whatever bread or other food he found in the house and give it in charity secretly on his way. And I heard him say: "If Allah has commanded us to give charity before consulting the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), then charity before intimate conversation with Him, the Exalted, is more excellent and more deserving of virtue."

Ahmad ibn Zuhayr ibn Harb said: My father related to us, Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Abu Hurairah and Ka'b met, and Abu Hurairah said: "Indeed on Jumu'ah there is an hour in which no Muslim man who is in prayer and asks Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for anything will fail to be given it." Ka'b said: "I will tell you about the day of Jumu'ah: when it comes, the heavens, the earth, the land, the sea, the mountains, the trees and all creatures are seized with dread of it, except the son of Adam and the devils. The angels surround the doors of the mosque and record whoever comes first, then the next, until the imam comes out. When the imam comes out, they fold up their scrolls. Whoever comes after that comes for the right of Allah, for what was prescribed upon him. It is an obligation upon every adult to bathe on that day as he bathes from major impurity (janabah). Charity on it is greater than charity on other days, and the sun has never risen or set on a day like the day of Jumu'ah." Ibn Abbas said: "This is the hadith of Ka'b and Abu Hurairah, and I think that if one's family has perfume, he should apply some of it."

**Twenty-sixth:** That it is the day on which Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, manifests Himself to His believing friends in Paradise, and they visit Him on it. So those nearest to Him will be nearest to the imam, and those who hasten most to the visit will be those who hasten most to the Jumu'ah. Yahya ibn Yaman related from Shuraik, from Abu al-Yaqzan, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, concerning the words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And with Us is more﴾ [Qaf 50:35], that he said: "He manifests Himself to them every Friday."

Al-Tabarani mentioned in his *Mu'jam* from the hadith of Abu Nu'aym al-Mas'udi, from al-Minhal ibn Amr, from Abu Ubaydah, who said: Abdullah (ibn Mas'ud) said: "Hasten to the Jumu'ah, for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, appears to the people of Paradise every Friday on a mound of camphor, and they are nearest to Him in proportion to their haste to the Jumu'ah. Then Allah, glorified is He, brings them a honour that they had not seen before. Then they return to their families and tell them about what Allah has brought upon them." He said: Then Abdullah entered the mosque and saw two men, and Abdullah said: "Two men, and I am the third; if Allah wills, He will bless the third."

Al-Bayhaqi mentioned in *Shu'ab al-Iman* from Alqamah ibn Qays, who said: I went out with Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, to a Jumu'ah, and he found three people had preceded him. He said: "The fourth of four, and the fourth of four is not far (away)." Then he said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Indeed people will sit on the Day of Resurrection in Allah's presence according to the earliness of their going to the Jumu'ah: the first, then the second, then the third, then the fourth.'" Then he said: "And the fourth of four is not far."

Al-Daraqutni said in his book *al-Ru'yah* (The Vision): Ahmad ibn Salman ibn al-Hasan related to us, Muhammad ibn Uthman ibn Muhammad related to us, Marwan ibn Ja'far related to us, Nafi' Abu al-Hasan, client of the Banu Hashim, related to us, Ata' ibn Abi Maymunah related to us, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, the believers will see their Lord, and the most recent to look upon Him will be the one who came early to the Jumu'ah every week, and the believing women will see Him on the day of Fitr and the day of Nahr."

Muhammad ibn Nuh related to us, Muhammad ibn Musa ibn Sufyan al-Sukkari related to us, Abdullah ibn al-Jahm al-Razi related to us, Amr ibn Abi Qays related to us, from Abu Tayyibah, from Asim, from Uthman ibn Umayr Abu al-Yaqzan, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said:

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 62, verses 9–10 (part 5 of 6):

"Jibril came to me holding something like a white mirror, in which there was something like a black spot. I said, 'What is this, Jibril?' He said, 'This is Friday, which Allah presents to you so that it may be a festival (ʿīd) for you and for your people after you.' I said, 'And what do we gain from it?' He said, 'You have good in it. You are the first in it, and the Jews and the Christians come after you. In it there is an hour in which no servant asks Allah, Mighty and Majestic, for anything that is destined for him except that He gives it to him, or, if it is not destined for him, He gives him something better than it. He protects him from the evil of what is written against him, or else He averts from him something even greater than that.' I said, 'And what is this black spot?' He said, 'It is the Hour, which will arise on a Friday. It is, for us, the lord of the days, and the people of the Hereafter call it the Day of Increase (yawm al-mazīd).' I said, 'O Jibril, and what is the Day of Increase?' He said, 'Your Lord, Mighty and Majestic, has taken in Paradise a wide valley of white musk. When Friday comes, He descends upon His Throne, and the Throne is surrounded by pulpits of light. The prophets come and sit upon them. Then the pulpits are surrounded by pulpits of gold, and the truthful ones (al-ṣiddīqūn) and the martyrs come and sit upon them, and the people of the chambers come and sit upon the dunes (kuthub). Then their Lord, Mighty and Majestic, manifests Himself to them.' He said, 'They look at Him, and He says: I am the One who fulfilled My promise to you and perfected My blessing upon you, and this is the place of My honour, so ask Me.' They ask Him for His good pleasure. He says: 'My pleasure has brought you down to My abode, and I am your honour, so ask Me.' They ask Him for His good pleasure. He said: 'He then testifies to them of His good pleasure. Then they keep asking Him until their desire is fulfilled. Then there is opened for them at that moment what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived.' He said: 'Then the Lord of Might ascends, and the prophets and the martyrs ascend with Him, and the people of the chambers return to their chambers. Each chamber is of pearl, without seam or break, or of a red ruby, or of a green emerald. Its doors, its upper rooms, its ceilings and its locks are of the same substance. Its rivers flow, its fruits hang low, and in it are their spouses and their servants.' He said: 'They have no greater need for anything than for the Day of Friday, so that they may increase in the honour of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and in gazing upon His Noble Face. That is the Day of Increase.'"

There are several chains of transmission for this hadith, which Abu al-Hasan al-Daraqutni mentioned in his book *al-Ru'ya* (The Vision).

The twenty-seventh point: the witness (shāhid) by which Allah swore in His Book has been explained as the Day of Friday. Ḥumayd ibn Zanjawayh said: Ḥaddathanā ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mūsā, Anbaʾanā Mūsā ibn ʿUbayda, from Ayyūb ibn Khālid, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rāfiʿ, from Abū Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The promised day is the Day of Resurrection, the witnessed day is the Day of ʿArafa, and the witness is the Day of Friday. The sun has not risen or set upon a day better than the Day of Friday. In it there is an hour in which no believing servant meets it while calling upon Allah for good, except that He answers him, or seeks refuge from evil, except that He protects him from it."

Al-Ḥārith ibn Abī Usāma narrated it in his *Musnad* from Rawḥ, from Mūsā ibn ʿUbayda.

In the *Muʿjam* of al-Ṭabarānī, through the narration of Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAyyāsh: Ḥaddathanī my father, Ḥaddathanī Ḍamḍam ibn Zurʿa, from Shurayḥ ibn ʿUbayd, from Abū Mālik al-Ashʿarī, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The promised day is the Day of Resurrection, the witness is the Day of Friday, and the witnessed day is the Day of ʿArafa. Allah has stored up the Day of Friday for us, and the middle prayer (ṣalāt al-wusṭā) is the ʿAṣr prayer." It has also been narrated through the hadith of Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim.

I say: The apparent meaning, and Allah knows best, is that this is the interpretation of Abū Hurayra. Imam Aḥmad said: Ḥaddathanā Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar, Ḥaddathanā Shuʿba, I heard ʿAlī ibn Zayd and Yūnus ibn ʿUbayd narrating from ʿAmmār, the client of the Banū Hāshim, from Abū Hurayra. As for ʿAlī ibn Zayd, he traced it back to the Prophet (ﷺ). As for Yūnus, he did not go beyond Abū Hurayra, that he said regarding this verse ﴿By the witness and the witnessed﴾: "The witness is the Day of Friday, the witnessed is the Day of ʿArafa, and the promised is the Day of Resurrection."

The twenty-eighth point: it is the day on which the heavens and the earth, the mountains and the seas, and all creation, except humans and jinn, are terrified. Abū al-Jawāb narrated from ʿAmmār ibn Zurayq, from Manṣūr, from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: Kaʿb and Abū Hurayra met, and Abū Hurayra said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "On Friday there is truly an hour in which no Muslim servant meets it while asking Allah for the good of this world and the Hereafter, except that He gives it to him."

Kaʿb said: "Shall I not tell you about the Day of Friday? When the Day of Friday comes, the heavens and the earth, the mountains and the seas, and all creation are terrified of it, except the son of Adam and the devils. The angels surround the doors of the mosques and write down the first, then the next, until the imam comes out. When the imam comes out, they fold up their scrolls. Whoever comes after that comes for the right of Allah and for what has been written for him. It is obligatory upon every person who has reached puberty (ḥālim) to bathe on it, as he bathes from major impurity (janāba). Charity on it is better than charity on all other days. The sun has not risen or set upon a day like the Day of Friday."

Ibn ʿAbbās said: "This is the hadith of Kaʿb and Abū Hurayra, and I see that whoever has perfume in his household should apply some of it on that day."

In the hadith of Abū Hurayra from the Prophet (ﷺ): "The sun does not rise or set upon a day better than the Day of Friday. There is no creature except that it is terrified on the Day of Friday, except these two species, the jinn and humankind." This is a sound hadith (ṣaḥīḥ).

This is because it is the day on which the Hour will arise, the world will be folded up, this world will be laid waste, and people will be raised to their abodes in Paradise or Hell.

The twenty-ninth point: it is the day which Allah has reserved for this community, and He led the People of the Book astray from it before them, as in the *Ṣaḥīḥ* (the two Ṣaḥīḥ collections) on the authority of Abū Hurayra from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The sun has not risen or set upon a day better than the Day of Friday. Allah guided us to it, and the people went astray from it. So the people follow us in it. It is ours, and for the Jews it is Saturday, and for the Christians it is Sunday." In another hadith it is: "Allah has reserved it for us."

Imam Aḥmad said: Ḥaddathanā ʿAlī ibn ʿĀṣim, from Ḥuṣayn ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿUmar ibn Qays, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ashʿath, from ʿĀʾisha, who said: "While I was with the Prophet (ﷺ), a Jewish man sought permission to enter. He was permitted, and he said, 'As-sām ʿalayka' (death be upon you). The Prophet (ﷺ) said, 'And upon you.' She said: I wanted to speak. Then he entered a second time and said the same, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said, 'And upon you.' She said: I wanted to speak. Then he entered a third time and said, 'As-sām ʿalaykum' (death be upon you all). She said: I said, 'Rather, death and the wrath of Allah be upon you, brothers of apes and swine! Do you greet the Messenger of Allah with what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did not greet him with?' She said: He looked at me and said, 'Mah (stop). Allah does not love obscenity nor vulgar speech.' They said a saying, and we returned it to them, and it did them no harm, and it will cling to them until the Day of Resurrection. They do not envy us for anything as they envy us for Friday, which Allah guided us to and they went astray from, and for the qibla which Allah guided us to and they went astray from, and for our saying 'Amīn' behind the imam."

In the *Ṣaḥīḥayn* from the hadith of Abū Hurayra from the Prophet (ﷺ): "We are the last and the first on the Day of Resurrection. Although they were given the Book before us, and we were given it after them, this is their day which was enjoined upon them, but they differed about it, so Allah guided us to it. The people are following us in it: the Jews tomorrow, and the Christians the day after tomorrow."

Regarding *bayda* (in the sense of "except" or "but"), there are two dialects: with the letter *bā'* (bayda), which is the well-known form, and *mayda* with *mīm*, which Abū ʿUbayd reported. This word has two meanings: the first is "other than" (ghayr), which is the more famous of its two meanings, and the second is "upon" (ʿalā). Abū ʿUbayd cited as evidence for this second meaning the verse of poetry:

*"I did that deliberately, though I think that if I had died, you would not wail (tarinnī) for me."*

*Tarinnī* means: you would wail, from *al-ranīn* (lamentation).

The thirtieth point: it is Allah's chosen day among the days of the week, just as the month of Ramadan is His chosen month among the months of the year, the Night of Power (laylat al-qadr) is His chosen night among the nights, Mecca is His chosen land among the lands, and Muḥammad (ﷺ) is His chosen one among His creation.

Ādam ibn Abī Iyās said: Ḥaddathanā Shaybān Abū Muʿāwiya, from ʿĀṣim ibn Abī al-Najūd, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Kaʿb al-Aḥbār, who said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, chose the months, and He chose the month of Ramadan. He chose the days, and He chose the Day of Friday. He chose the nights, and He chose the Night of Power. He chose the hours, and He chose the hour of prayer. The Friday prayer expiates what is between it and the next Friday, and adds three days. Ramadan expiates what is between it and the next Ramadan. Hajj expiates what is between it and the next Hajj. ʿUmra expiates what is between it and the next ʿUmra. A man dies between two good deeds: a good deed he has performed, and a good deed he awaits, meaning two prayers. The devils are chained in Ramadan, the gates of Hell are closed, the gates of Paradise are opened, and it is said in it: 'O seeker of good, come forward!' Ramadan is complete, and there are no nights more beloved to Allah for deeds than the nights of the last ten."

The thirty-first point: the souls of the dead draw near to their graves and meet them on the Day of Friday. They recognise their visitors and whoever passes by them, and they greet them. They meet them on that day more than they know them on other days. It is a day on which the living and the dead meet. When the Hour arises on it, the first and the last will meet, and the people of the earth and the people of the heavens, the Lord and the servant, the doer and his deed, the oppressed and his oppressor, the sun and the moon, which had never met before. It is the day of gathering and meeting. For this reason people meet more in this world on it than on any other day, so it is the Day of Meeting (yawm al-talāqī).

Abū al-Tayyāḥ Yazīd ibn Ḥumayd said: Muṭarrif ibn ʿAbd Allāh used to hasten to enter (the cemetery) every Friday. He set out in the night until, when he was at the graves on a Friday, he said: "I saw the owner of every grave sitting upon his grave. They said, 'This is Muṭarrif, who comes on Friday.' I said to them, 'Do you know Friday among you?' They said, 'Yes, and we know what the birds say about it.' I said, 'And what do the birds say about it?' They said, 'They say: O Lord, grant safety, safety; it is a righteous day.'"

Ibn Abī al-Dunyā mentioned in his book *al-Manāmāt* (Dreams) and elsewhere, from some of the people of ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī, who said: "I saw ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī in my dream two years after his death. I said, 'Did you not die?' He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'Where are you?' He said, 'By Allah, I am in a garden of the gardens of Paradise, I and a group of my companions. We gather every Friday night and the morning after it at Bakr ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Muzanī, and we receive your news.' I said, 'Are your bodies or your souls?' He said, 'Far from it! The bodies have decayed, and only the souls meet.' I said, 'Do you know of our visiting you?' He said, 'We know of it on Friday evening, all of Friday, and the Saturday night until sunrise.' I said, 'How is that, when it is not so on all other days?' He said, 'Because of the excellence and greatness of the Day of Friday.'"

Ibn Abī al-Dunyā also mentioned from Muḥammad ibn Wāsiʿ that he used to go every Saturday morning to the cemetery (al-jabbāna), stand at the graves, greet them, pray for them, and then leave. It was said to him, "If only you would make this day Monday." He said, "It has reached me that the dead know of their visitors on Friday, the day before it, and the day after it."

He also mentioned, from Sufyān al-Thawrī, who said: "It has reached me from al-Ḍaḥḥāk that he said: Whoever visits a grave on Saturday before sunrise, the dead person knows of his visit." It was said to him, "How is that?" He said, "Because of the position of the Day of Friday."

The thirty-second matter: it is disliked to single out Friday for fasting. This is the explicit position of Ahmad. Al-Athram said: It was said to Abu 'Abd Allah (Ahmad): Is fasting on Friday permitted? He mentioned the hadith prohibiting that it be singled out, then said: "Except if it is part of a fast he was already accustomed to keep. But singling it out, no." I said: "A man who used to fast every other day, and whose fast-days happened to fall so that he did not fast on Thursday, fasted on Friday, and did not fast on Saturday, so that Friday stood alone?" He said: "That is fine, unless he deliberately fasts it specifically. It is only disliked to deliberately fast Friday."

Malik and Abu Hanifa permitted fasting it like other days.

Malik said: "I have not heard anyone of knowledge, understanding, and those who are followed, forbid fasting on Friday. Fasting it is good. I have seen some people of knowledge fast it, and I think he was deliberately choosing it."

Ibn 'Abd al-Barr said: The reports from the Prophet (ﷺ) about fasting on Friday differ. Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) "used to fast three days of every month," and said: "I rarely saw him break his fast on a Friday." This is a sahih hadith.

It has also been narrated from Ibn 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him and his father) that he said: "I never once saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) break his fast on a Friday."

Ibn Abi Shayba mentioned it from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, from 'Umayr ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Ibn 'Umar.

Ibn 'Abbas narrated that he used to fast it and was consistent in doing so.

Ibn Jarir mentioned, from Mughira, from Ibrahim (al-Nakha'i), that they disliked fasting Friday so that they would have strength for the prayer.

I say: The grounds for disliking it are three. This is the first. But it poses a difficulty: the dislike disappears if a day is added before it or after it to the fast.

The second: it is a day of 'Id (festival), and this is what the Prophet (ﷺ) pointed to. Two objections have been raised against this reasoning. The first: fasting it is not forbidden, whereas fasting on the day of 'Id is forbidden. The second: the dislike disappears when it is not singled out. The answer to both objections is that it is not the annual 'Id, but the weekly 'Id, and the prohibition applies only to fasting the annual 'Id.

As for when a person fasts a day before it or a day after it, he has not fasted it because it is Friday and an 'Id, so the harm arising from singling it out disappears; rather, it is included in his fasting as a subordinate element. On this basis is to be understood what Imam Ahmad (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated in his *Musnad*, and al-Nasa'i and al-Tirmidhi from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, if it is sahih: "I rarely saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) break his fast on a Friday."

If this is sound, it must be interpreted to mean that he would include it in his fasting as a subordinate element, not that he would single it out, because the prohibition against that is authentic.

And where are the prohibitive hadiths established in the *Two Sahihs* in comparison with this permissive report, which no one among the people of the Sahih collections narrated, and which al-Tirmidhi judged to be gharib (rare)? How can the clear, authentic hadiths be set against it, and then this be given precedence over them?!

The third ground: blocking the means (sadd al-dhari'a, blocking the pathways to what is prohibited), lest people add to the religion what is not in it, and lest it lead to imitating the People of the Book in singling out certain days for complete abstention from worldly activities. Added to this meaning: since this day has apparent excellence over other days, the motive to fast it is strong, so people are likely to follow one another in fasting it and celebrating it more than they celebrate fasting any other day. In that is the attaching to the Sharia of what is not from it. For this reason, Allah knows best, the Prophet (ﷺ) forbade singling out the night of Friday for standing in prayer above other nights, because it is among the most excellent nights, to the point that some scholars preferred it over Laylat al-Qadr, and a narration from Ahmad was transmitted to that effect. It is thus a likely pathway to singling it out for worship, so the Lawgiver closed off this means and blocked it by prohibiting singling it out for standing in prayer. And Allah knows best.

If it is said: What do you say about singling out another day for fasting?

It is said: As for singling out what the Lawgiver singled out, such as Monday, the Day of 'Arafah, and the Day of 'Ashura, that is Sunna. As for singling out other days, such as Saturday, Tuesday, Sunday, and Wednesday, that is disliked.

And whatever of these is closer to imitating the disbelievers, by singling out their festival days for veneration and fasting, is more strongly disliked and closer to being prohibited.

The thirty-third matter: it is the day of the gathering of people and of reminding them of the origin (al-mabda') and the return (al-ma'ad). Allah, glorified and exalted, has prescribed for every community in the week a day on which they devote themselves to worship and gather to remember the origin and the return, the reward and the punishment, and they remember through it their gathering on the Great Day of Assembly, standing before the Lord of the worlds. The most fitting of the days for this purpose is the day on which Allah gathers all creation, and that is Friday. Allah reserved it for this Ummah because of its merit and nobility. So He prescribed their gathering on this day for obedience to Him, and He ordained their gathering on it along with the other nations to attain His honor. It is the day of gathering by Sharia in this world, and by decree in the Hereafter. And at the measure of its midpoint, at the time of the sermon and the prayer, the people of Paradise are in their abodes and the people of the Fire are in their abodes, as was established from Ibn Mas'ud through more than one route, that he said: "The day will not reach its midpoint on the Day of Resurrection until the people of Paradise take their midday rest in their abodes and the people of the Fire in their abodes," and he recited: ﴿The companions of the Garden on that Day will have a better resting place and a finer place of repose﴾ [al-Furqan: 24].

And he recited: "Then indeed their place of repose is toward the Hellfire," and it is thus in his recitation.

As for the fact that the days are seven, this is known only by the nations that have a Book. As for a nation that has no Book, it knows this only from those who received it from them, from the nations of the prophets, because there is no perceptible sign by which it can be known that the days are seven, unlike the month and the year and their seasons. When Allah created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days, and made Himself known to His servants through His messengers and prophets, He prescribed for them a day in the week to remind them of that, of the wisdom of creation and what they were created for, of the appointed term of the world, the folding up of the heavens and the earth, and the return of the affair as He began it, a promise binding upon Him, and a true word.

For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) used to recite in the dawn prayer on Friday the two surahs *Alif-Lam-Mim Tanzil* and *Hal ata 'ala al-insan* (Surah al-Insan), because of what these two surahs include of what has been and will be concerning the origin and the return, the gathering of creation and their resurrection from the graves to Paradise and the Fire. Not for the sake of the prostration, as one imagines who lacks knowledge and understanding, so he performs a prostration from another surah, believing that the dawn of Friday was given preference by a prostration, and he denounces whoever does not do so.

Likewise was his recitation (ﷺ) at great gatherings, such as the festivals and the like: he recited the surah that contains tawhid, the origin and the return, the stories of the prophets with their peoples, and what Allah did to those who denied them and disbelieved in them of destruction and misery, and those who believed in them and affirmed them of salvation and well-being.

As he recited in the two 'Eids the surahs *Qaf, wal-Qur'an al-majid* and *Iqtarabat al-sa'a wa-nshaqqa al-qamar*, and at times *Sabbih isma rabbika al-a'la* and *Hal ataka hadith al-ghashiya*.

And at times he recited on Friday the Surah al-Jumu'a, because of what it contains of the command to this prayer, the obligation to hasten toward it, and abandoning trade that prevents it, and the command to increase the remembrance of Allah so that they may attain success in both abodes, for forgetting His remembrance brings ruin and destruction in both abodes.
